blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
In practice, automation and digital transformation projects fail for the same small reasons over and over. People were not involved early. The process being automated was broken to begin with. Success was never clearly defined. And nobody owned the change once the launch was over.

A good intermediate leader fixes each of these before writing a single line of code. She involves the people whose work will change. She fixes the process first, then automates it. She defines success in numbers. And she makes sure somebody, specifically named, is still responsible three months after go-live.

Automation works when the process underneath it is already working. Transformation works when the people inside it are already ready. Skip either step, and even the best technology produces an expensive disappointment.

items.q: According to the text, why do automation projects fail?
options: Because budgets are always too small
Because the technology is rarely good enough
For the same small reasons over and over
items.why: "projects fail for the same small reasons over and over" — são causas repetidas, não a tecnologia.

items.q: What does the good leader do FIRST, before automating?
items.why: "She fixes the process first, then automates it."

items.q: How should success be defined, according to the text?
options: By the size of the team
items.why: "She defines success in numbers."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Someone must own the change after go-live.
Good technology alone does not guarantee success.
People should be involved before the work changes.
Automating a broken process still delivers real value.
items.why: Inferência: o texto insiste que a automação só funciona se o processo já funciona — automatizar algo quebrado gera decepção cara.

items.q: The phrase "specifically named" suggests that…
options: the software should carry the person's name
the owner must have a senior job title
the launch date should be public
vague, shared responsibility is not enough
items.why: Inferência: exigir um nome específico é o oposto de deixar a responsabilidade difusa — se é de todos, não é de ninguém.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie explicando como está resgatando o projeto. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, this is the second time we're trying to automate this workflow, and I want us to do it differently. Last time, nobody talked to the people who actually run the process. We built a tool for a process none of us really understood.

The first thing I did was sit with the team for two days and map what they actually do — not what the old diagram says they do. And honestly, the process itself was broken. There were three manual approvals that added nothing except delay. So before we touch any code, we're cutting those.

Second, success. Last time, success just meant "the system went live." That's not success — that's a switch being flicked. This time, success is measured: forty percent fewer manual steps, and invoices cleared in two days instead of nine.

And here's what changed everything for me. I've asked Marco to own this after go-live. Not the vendor, not "the team" — Marco, by name, for three months. If something breaks in week ten, we all know exactly who is picking it up.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What did nobody do the first time the project was attempted?
options: Talk to the people who run the process
items.why: "nobody talked to the people who actually run the process."

items.q: What did Sophie discover when she mapped the real process?
options: It was broken, with pointless manual approvals
It matched the old diagram exactly
items.why: "the process itself was broken. There were three manual approvals that added nothing except delay."

items.q: How is success measured this time?
options: By the system simply going live
By fewer manual steps and faster invoice clearing
By the number of people trained
By the cost of the vendor
items.why: "forty percent fewer manual steps, and invoices cleared in two days instead of nine."

items.q: When Sophie says "that's a switch being flicked," she means the old definition of success was…
items.why: Inferência: ligar o sistema é um evento, não um resultado — não prova que algo melhorou.

items.q: Why does Sophie insist on naming Marco specifically?
options: Because Marco built the original system
So Marco can approve the budget
So responsibility is clear if something breaks later
items.why: Inferência: nomear uma pessoa evita a responsabilidade difusa — "we all know exactly who is picking it up."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "She made sure to involve the team before designing the tool." To involve means to…
items.why: Involve = envolver, trazer as pessoas para dentro do processo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Automating a ___ only makes the same mistakes happen faster."
items.why: Broken process = processo quebrado; automatizá-lo só acelera os erros.

items.q: "Marco will own this after go-live." To own here means to…
items.why: To own (a change) = ser o responsável por ela, responder pelo resultado.

items.q: Go-live is best described as…
options: the moment the system starts running in production
items.why: Go-live = entrada em produção, quando o sistema passa a rodar de verdade.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Even the best technology produces an expensive ___ if the process is broken."
items.why: Disappointment = decepção; a tecnologia não entrega o resultado esperado e ainda custa caro.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em projetos de automação e transformação. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "We can't roll out the tool until the process is fixed." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implantar de forma progressiva, colocar em uso.

items.q: "The finance director still has to sign off on the new workflow." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Two managers pushed back on automating the approvals." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente vetar de vez.

items.q: "The team agreed to name an owner but never followed through." They…
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui, não levaram.

items.q: "Flicking the switch alone won't move the needle on delivery times." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
